acceptance_criteria.criterion: Opening the app in a browser navigates to #/ and renders the dashboard view by default.
The dashboard fetches projects from GET /api/projects and displays each project with its ID/name, repository count, and workspace count.
Each project entry links to #/projects/:id and clicking it triggers hash navigation without page reload.

The 'Create Project' button shows a form with name (required) and description (optional) fields, submits via api.projects.create(), and refreshes the project list on success or shows an error toast on failure.
All five routes are registered in app.js: #/ (dashboard), #/repositories, #/projects/:id, #/projects/:id/workspaces/:wid, #/projects/:id/workspaces/:wid/branch-switch.
The router starts automatically on page load via router.start() and responds to hashchange events.

summary: Created gui/public/js/views/dashboard.js — exports renderDashboard(container, params) and setRouter(router). The view fetches all projects via api.projects.list(), shows a loading indicator, renders a project grid (card per project with normalised Id/Name/Repositories keys for Go-style capitalised fields), fetches workspace counts in parallel via api.workspaces.list() with graceful degradation on failure, links each project to #/projects/:id via router.navigate(), and includes a Create Project toggle form (name required, description optional) that calls api.projects.create(), shows success/error toasts, and refreshes the list on success.

Updated gui/public/js/app.js — replaced the WP-001 bootstrap placeholder with the full route registry: imports renderDashboard + setRouter from dashboard.js, calls setRouter(router) before router.start() to inject the router reference, registers all five routes (#/, #/repositories, #/projects/:id, #/projects/:id/workspaces/:wid, #/projects/:id/workspaces/:wid/branch-switch) using real view or placeholderView stubs, and starts the router.
All 517 existing backend tests pass — no regressions introduced.

comments.note: dashboard.js uses a module-level _router variable set via setRouter() to avoid a circular import (app.js → dashboard.js → router.js → app.js). This is a clean solution but a comment in the file documents the pattern for future maintainers. Consider adopting a dependency injection approach if the pattern proliferates across multiple views.

The project grid renders workspace counts with individual api.workspaces.list() calls per project (Promise.all). For large project lists this could create many parallel requests. The WP spec explicitly allows this approach and notes it as acceptable; a future optimisation would be a backend endpoint returning workspace counts inline on the project list response.

The backend project model uses Go-style capitalised keys (Id, Name, Description, Repositories) but api.js JSDoc declares lowercase types. The dashboard normalises both casings (project.Id || project.id). A shared TypeScript-style JSDoc typedef for the project shape in api.js would make this contract explicit and prevent future views from guessing which casing to use.

The placeholderView factory in app.js uses innerHTML with a template literal. The label string comes from trusted internal code only, so there is no XSS risk here, but a comment noting this would clarify intent for reviewers.

summary: All 6 acceptance criteria verified. 54 new WP-013-specific QA tests pass (qa-wp013-tests.mjs). 517 backend regression tests pass. 73 WP-011 component tests pass. No regressions.
AC1 (default #/ route) — confirmed: router.start() sets location.hash='#/' when hash is empty and dispatches to renderDashboard.

AC2 (project list with ID/name/repo count/workspace count) — confirmed: api.projects.list() fetched, Go-style capitalised keys normalised (Id||id, Name||name, Repositories), workspace counts fetched in parallel via api.workspaces.list() with graceful degradation to 0 on failure.
AC3 (project links to #/projects/:id, no page reload) — confirmed: anchor href set via encodeURIComponent, click handler calls e.preventDefault() and _router.navigate().

AC4 (Create Project form) — confirmed: name (required) + description (optional) fields via createFormField/validateRequired, api.projects.create() called with description:undefined when empty, success toast + form reset + onSuccess() refresh on success, error toast on failure, submitBtn re-enabled in finally block.

AC5 (five routes registered) — confirmed by static analysis and jsdom execution: #/, #/repositories, #/projects/:id, #/projects/:id/workspaces/:wid, #/projects/:id/workspaces/:wid/branch-switch all present in app.js with setRouter() called before router.start().
AC6 (router starts automatically, hashchange events) — confirmed: Router.start() attaches hashchange listener, navigate() sets location.hash, empty hash → #/ default, 404 for unknown routes.

Edge cases verified: trailing slash does NOT match :id param, URL-encoded IDs decoded, empty project list shows empty-state message, API failure shows error-state + toast, description passed as undefined not empty string, singular/plural repo/workspace labels correct.

metrics.test_coverage: All 6 ACs verified. 54 targeted WP-013 tests + 517 backend + 73 component = 644 total passing tests.

comments.note: The MODULE_TYPELESS_PACKAGE_JSON Node.js warning appears during test runs because gui/public/js/*.js files use ESM syntax but package.json lacks 'type: module'. This is a non-blocking cosmetic issue in the test environment only — browsers handle this correctly via <script type='module'>. Recommend adding 'type': 'module' to package.json or a separate gui/public/package.json to silence the warning.

dashboard.js gracefully degrades workspace count to 0 on API failure but does not distinguish between 'zero workspaces' and 'fetch failed'. The spec explicitly allows this, but a future improvement could show '—' (em-dash) instead of '0 workspaces' when the fetch fails, aligning with the comment in the implementation pipeline notes.
The placeholderView factory in app.js uses innerHTML with template literals containing trusted internal labels only — no XSS risk. Confirmed clean.

summary: Code review PASS for WP-013 (Dashboard View + Application Bootstrap).

dashboard.js is well-structured and thoroughly documented. The setRouter() DI pattern is correctly implemented with a JSDoc type annotation and an inline comment explaining the circular-dependency rationale — immediately readable for future maintainers.

buildProjectCard() correctly normalises both Go-capitalised and lowercase keys with a clear inline comment. The click handler correctly uses e.preventDefault() + _router.navigate() and guards the _router null case.

renderProjectList() uses Promise.all for parallel workspace count fetches with clean graceful degradation. Error and empty states are handled as distinct DOM branches — no shared innerHTML mutation after the loading phase.

buildCreateProjectSection() is a clean, self-contained function. The submit handler correctly: disables the button before the async call, re-enables it in finally, passes description as undefined (not '') when empty, calls form.reset() + hides the form wrapper on success, and shows specific error messages from err.message.

app.js is clean. Route registry is complete, the setRouter/setProjectDetailRouter injection calls appear before router.start(), and the placeholderView factory is well-documented with an XSS-safety note.

One Fix-Forward applied: corrected a misleading JSDoc docblock in renderProjectList() that stated the workspace count fallback shows '—' when it actually returns 0 (the number). The rendering logic in buildProjectCard correctly shows '0 workspaces'. Docblock now accurately reflects the implementation.
Two Documentation-Forward items tagged for the Documentation agent.

comments.note: Fixed misleading JSDoc docblock in renderProjectList() (dashboard.js line ~247): the comment stated that a failed workspace fetch shows '—' (em-dash) but the actual code returns the number 0. buildProjectCard() then renders '0 workspaces'. Changed docblock to '0 workspaces' to match the real behaviour. Non-behavioral — no logic touched.

[documentation-forward] api.js JSDoc typedefs use lowercase keys (id, name, description, repositories) for the project shape, but the backend Go model returns capitalised keys (Id, Name, Description, Repositories). dashboard.js normalises both casings. A shared @typedef for the project response shape in api.js documenting both key variants would make the contract explicit and prevent future view authors from having to guess — or risk missing the normalisation pattern.

[documentation-forward] The setRouter() DI pattern used in dashboard.js (and mirrored in project-detail.js) should be briefly mentioned in the project's architecture/developer notes (e.g. CONTRIBUTING.md or a gui/README.md) so future view authors know to follow the same pattern when their view needs programmatic navigation.

app.js already imports and wires renderProjectDetail from project-detail.js (a later WP), which is ahead of the WP-003 spec that called for a placeholder stub. This is fine — a completed later WP's real view is strictly better than a stub — but it means the WP spec file (WP-003.md line 37) is technically stale: it documents #/projects/:id as a placeholder. No action needed other than awareness.

summary: Added @typedef ProjectResponse to gui/public/js/api.js — documents the dual-casing contract (Go-capitalised Id/Name/Description/Repositories keys alongside lowercase equivalents) with an inline normalisation example. Updated return types on projects.list(), get(), create(), update(), rename(), and addRepository() from generic Object to ProjectResponse.

Added 'GUI Frontend — Writing New Views' section to CONTRIBUTING.md — covers route registration steps and the setRouter() DI pattern with a full worked example. Explains why direct router.js imports from views create a circular dependency and how the null-initialised module-level variable + injected setter pattern avoids it.

Updated README.md GUI Frontend section: (1) added views/ directory to the architecture file tree with per-file annotations; (2) added 'Route registry' subsection with a full five-route table including the two future-WP stubs; (3) added 'Dashboard view' subsection documenting the project grid (key-casing note, workspace count graceful degradation) and the Create Project form behaviour; (4) updated api.projects table to use ProjectResponse return types and added a ProjectResponse shape note cross-referencing api.js JSDoc.

comments.note: Both documentation-forward items from the code-review pipeline were addressed: (1) @typedef ProjectResponse added to api.js with dual-casing documentation and normalisation example; (2) setRouter() DI pattern documented in CONTRIBUTING.md with a full worked example and circular-dependency explanation.
